result:
The fix is in place and verified.

`PostController.destroy` (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:99`) loaded the post and deleted it without ever consulting the policy — the only mutating action missing an `this.authorize()` call. I added `await this.authorize('delete', [Post, post])` right after `findOrFail`, matching the shape `update`/`edit` already use. No policy change was needed: `PostPolicy.delete` (`app/Policies/PostPolicy.ts:29`) already returned `user !== null && Number(user.id) === post.authorId`, and the `posts.destroy` route was already behind the `auth` middleware, so guests keep the framework's usual unauthenticated handling while a signed-in non-author now gets a 403 and the row survives. I also added `tests/PostDestroy.test.ts`, a feature test covering all three cases (non-author 403 + post still present, guest refused + post still present, author's own delete still works); it migrates the `NODE_ENV=test` SQLite database and reuses its two fixture users by email rather than resetting the file, so it is safe to re-run and does not clobber anything else in the suite. `bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` is 5/5 green across two consecutive runs.
